history.contentIn: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) is a proposed solar radiation modification method that would introduce aerosols into the stratosphere to reflect a small fraction of incoming sunlight, analogous in mechanism to cooling after large volcanic eruptions such as Mount Pinatubo in 1991. The IPCC has described SAI as the most-researched solar geoengineering approach and notes that, used at moderate intensity, it could limit warming, but imperfectly and with other possible effects if used suboptimally. Candidate materials discussed in the literature include sulfates and, in some proposals, calcite or other particles. Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) depend on sea ice as a platform for hunting seals. Arctic sea ice has declined in extent and thickness over the satellite era as the Arctic has warmed about twice as fast as the global mean (Arctic amplification). The IUCN and Arctic scientists treat loss of sea-ice hunting habitat as the primary long-term threat to the species. Some subpopulations have been relatively stable or better counted in recent surveys, which deniers sometimes quote as 'polar bears are fine.' That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range. Polar-bear numbers are not a single global census with low error; management units differ. Conservation hunting quotas and pollution are additional pressures, but they do not make sea-ice loss irrelevant. There is no scientific basis for the claim that polar bears are thriving because of chemtrails or that global warming is a hoax because one subpopulation increased.

Some subpopulations have been relatively stable or better counted in recent surveys, which deniers sometimes quote as 'polar bears are fine.' That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range. Polar-bear numbers are not a single global census with low error; management units differ. Conservation hunting quotas and pollution are additional pressures, but they do not make sea-ice loss irrelevant. There is no scientific basis for the claim that polar bears are thriving because of chemtrails or that global warming is a hoax because one subpopulation increased.
